observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of a bed of burning charcoal/ember chunks. Several dark, cracked, roughly cylindrical and angular pieces sit in a fixed pile, with a persistent orange glow seeping from the gaps and lower edges. Over and around these pieces, bright yellow flame tongues and dense streams of fine sparks swirl continuously against an otherwise black background. A large rounded, surface-cracked coal on the right side of the frame and the lower foreground chunks keep the same positions throughout, indicating the camera is essentially stationary relative to the coals.
visible_changes: The yellow flame mass deforms and shifts location frame to frame: at t=0.00 it is a plume on the right, by t=0.13–0.20 it collapses into a bright central blob, then elongates into a horizontal ribbon across the middle (t=0.33–0.60), and later rises as a vertical column on the left/center (t=1.20–2.00) before spreading again.

Streams of sparks (thin bright yellow streaks) repeatedly erupt, fan out—often toward the upper-left and left—and fade, with their density and direction varying: heavy leftward spraying around t=0.60–1.00, a calmer period with fewer streaks around t=1.30–1.60, then renewed dense spraying from t=1.90 to the end.
Individual spark streaks translate across the frame (e.g., long diagonal streaks crossing the right coal and the lower chunks in the later frames), distinct from the flame's own deformation.

Overall brightness of the flame pulses—flaring into a saturated yellow core at certain moments (t=0.13, t=1.27, t=1.94) and dimming to wispy translucent tongues at others—while the underlying orange ember glow and the positions of the coal chunks remain steady.
The motion is already ongoing at the first sampled frame and is still ongoing at the last; no start, contact, or completion of the burning/sparking is shown within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initially ignited the coals or what (if anything) is disturbing them to produce the spark bursts.
Whether the spark activity is continuous or intermittent outside the sampled window.
The exact fuel/coal type and the full extent of the fire beyond the tight frame.
uncertain_details: Minor camera shake or drift cannot be fully excluded, but the fixed positions of the charcoal chunks argue against deliberate panning.
Distinguishing flame deformation from spark translation is partly ambiguous where streaks overlap the glowing flame body.
The precise cause of each spark burst (airflow, settling, etc.) is not visible and is not inferred.
